summary: Partial trace grouping breaks after sampling-rate toggle causing alert evaluation noise
description:
Issue summary:
Users report that after we flipped the global trace-sampling toggle (rollout 2026-03-09), traces in the Console timeline stop reliably inheriting parent.trace_id for a subset of sessions. Impact:
- Alert evaluation for 'error-rate by trace-group' produced a sudden set of noisy spikes the morning of 2026-03-10 (vectorpay-prod).
- Affected dashboards show duplicate/fragmented trace sessions which inflate per-session error counts and trigger P1 alerts.
Environment:
- prod-us-east (dedicated tenant for VectorPay)
- Ingest pipeline version: trace-ingest@v2.7.1
- Console/front-end: console@2026.03.08
Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Send high-volume requests with client-side sampling header X-Trace-Sample toggling between 0 and 1 every ~15s.
2) Observe Console -> Traces -> Timeline for a transaction group and corresponding Alert (error-rate by trace-group) firing.
Observed behavior:
- Trace fragments appear as separate trace groups (missing parent linkage) in the timeline.
- Alert evaluation window treats fragments as independent sessions and aggregates error ratios incorrectly, creating false positives.
Expected behavior:
- Sampling toggles should still preserve trace correlation keys so Console groups spans from the same logical session together.
Logs & artifacts:
- Example trace IDs and request IDs included in attachments (customer log bundle).
- Ingest logs show intermittent drop of 'parent_id' field for ~7% of sampled spans between 2026-03-09 22:10 and 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC.
- Alert eval snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/alerts/snapshots/alerts-2026-03-10-vectorpay.json
Business impact:
- Customer-facing alerts escalated to on-call SRE and customer success; VectorPay temporarily disabled an automated rollback config to mute alerts, impacting reliability testing.
Temporary workaround:
- Customer temporarily pinned trace-sampling to previous stable value and reverted the rollout. This reduced noise but degraded sampling coverage.
Next steps (engineering):
- Reproduce with internal loadgen under same sampling toggle cadence.
- Investigate ingest pipeline transform that normalizes parent_id and sampling headers (trace-collector).
- Determine if UI grouping logic tolerates missing parent_id by using correlation fields (session_id, request_id) as fallback.
- Prepare a hotfix to preserve parent_id on sampling transitions and add alert eval guard to ignore groups with <N spans.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: toggling sampling rate during high-throughput windows races with the step that attaches parent_id to spans. When sticky sampling state flips mid-session, collector can emit spans without parent_id which UI grouping then treats as new root traces. Repro in staging with loadgen toggling at 10-30s cadence reproduces ~5% fragment rate. Observed that a recent change in trace-collector v2.7.1 moved sampling flag update earlier in pipeline for performance; reverting ordering eliminates fragments in staging. Impacted component: trace-collector parent assignment ordering.
resolution_summary: (Work in progress) Temporary mitigation applied by customer (pin sampling). Engineering patch PR created to reorder sticky-sampling mutation after parent_id assignment (see PR). Plan: canary patch on prod-ingest tomorrow 2026-03-13, monitor for fragment rate <0.1%. Follow-up: add unit test and alert-eval guard to ignore groups with <3 spans in 5m window while patch rolls out.
